definitions.sender_class: class of the account that SENT a DeFiHackLabs-listed tx: attacker (the exploiter), bot (MEV searcher / copier / front-runner / arbitrage bot that raced or replayed the exploit), whitehat (rescuer or security firm), unknown (sender cannot be placed). tx_role 'non-attack' marks listed hashes that are not attack txs (approve, init, refund batch); they join no aggregate.
definitions.rule_order: tx override -> address registry (incident files, literature and anonymous-sender research, DHL header) -> R1 (>=1000 prior txs, tx index 0, coinbase payment or >=100 gwei tip -> bot, low) -> R1b (>=1000 prior txs, recurs in >=2 rows, pays coinbase -> bot, low) -> R2 (>=1000 prior txs and >=2000 now, no searcher signature -> unknown, low) -> R3 (DHL names attackers, sender is not one, did not deploy the attack contract, absent from the PoC source -> unknown, low) -> default attacker (medium if sender is the DHL attacker AND deployed the attack contract AND <1000 prior txs; else low).  Registry hits are high confidence.
definitions.mixed_rows: A row may list an attacker tx and a bot tx.  The attacker's tx (earliest non-pure-deploy) drives every attacker-side statistic; the bot's tx goes to the bot-side table.  If a row lists ONLY bot / whitehat / non-attack txs, the attacker's own tx is unlisted: attacker-side fields are 'not measured' and the row is excluded from attacker aggregates (it stays in the bot-side table).
